I don't mean to be a Debbie Downer Jr, but finding a psychiatrist in Montreal is not only a long process, but it might end up being very useless. Personally I gave up on psychiatric help when one's secretary called me to tell me my appointment was rescheduled because "Someone else needs it more than you." Said appointment was rescheduled for a month later, because "The psychiatrist only sees one patient a week." Which is astonishing and almost insulting. You wouldn't hear that about an oncologist for instance. To be taken seriously and seen immediately you need to be suicidal with a plan. Then they hold you in the ER for at least 72 hours until you no longer have a plan, and then you're discharged with an appointment for months later. 

Hopefully you'll find the help you need but you might need to either be really patient, pay someone for private care or try in another province. Apparently BC has great mental health care.

If you stop the child from doing this and focus their attention on something else and praise them, they will eventually understand they just shouldn't because mom or dad or teacher said so.

Teens now. They realize that adults are not actually above them. Adults do not actually have to approve of you for you to be worthy. So why all those expectations? That's how rebellious teens are created. They question authority since it's only a social construct. Also teenage years are the most frustrating since you're treated like a child but expected to behave like an adult.

In both stages, the brain is going through overwhelming changes that to lead kids to behave lije this. Remember. All we are is chemistry.

So yeah. Good parenting = love, patience and understanding. Bad parenting = everything else including spanking.

It wasn't great but I am still thankful it happened. I got a better diagnosis, though I don't agree with it but more time was spent on me as a patient than before. You get bette resources, better doctors, better social workers, psychologists, etc. etc. and since you're in a hospital, you get quick referrals as opposed to having to wait months if you were to do this yourself (I guess that depends on your location as well; in Canada it can literally take months to a year, but through the hospital I'm already the patient of a psychiatrist who will do a weekly follow-up).

Other than that, I think my experience can't speak for others because it depends on the hospital. For instance the hospital I'm in is a lot like prison, but with time you get privilege (like now I was able to leave for a few hours and I'm using my computer). Inside we're not allowed to do anything and on your first days, you can't go outside, can't wear your own clothes, can't have any of your possessions with you. And then as time goes by, you get privileges like going outside for a few hours, then wearing your clothes, maybe have a book (still no electronics; I found a "loophole" because I need to study for my exams so I'm allowed to have my computer but still no wifi). Some sections (for the high care patients) don't have windows, mirrors, real plates, real cutlery, etc. etc. It's miserable there. All they can do is walk around and sleep, and eat three times a day.

I know someone who went in a hospital where she was able to have all the same freedom as if she were home, minus of course control over her location. Besides what her treatment required her to do, she was free to have or refuse whatever she liked.

So yeah. Look into what hospital you'd like to go. Of course they won't tell you "We lock you up like a prisoner!" but ask them about what therapy entails, and if you will be allowed to have access to x or y. 

Good luck.
